correctness.rationale: The critical boundary lemma is verified directly from the floor mechanical coding: a Sturmian singular phase has precisely two labels, differing at j-1,j with 01 and 10 exchanged; a nonsingular phase has only one. For w_n=u_n XOR v_n, the sign is g_alpha(x+n alpha)g_beta(y+n beta), apart from finitely many boundary terms. Equidistribution for (alpha,beta) on the torus gives A_alpha=e^(2pi ix)*(1-e^(2pi i alpha))/(pi i)*(1-2beta) and the symmetric A_beta; irrationality makes both constants nonzero. Equal output therefore forces both phases equal. Two labeled input pairs cancel only when both phases are singular at the same index j, which yields exactly two parity classes, each of cardinality two, along one joint-phase orbit; their two output orbits differ at sites -1,0 and cannot coincide under a nonzero shift because of rational independence. Almost-everywhere injective factor of the uniquely ergodic torus rotation establishes the measure spectrum, with topological minimality from joint irrationality and open phase cylinders. The 101-site and 30000-term checks are illustrative, not a proof of global fibres.
